notes:
Summary: EmberWave is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for inference of several healthtech features: patient triage chat, clinical note embeddings for semantic search, and reranking of candidate answers in guided workflows. They are very security-sensitive (PHI potential) and require VPC + KMS + EU residency for certain datasets. Short-hand CRM notes below.

Key quote: "Need predictable per-token economics with p99 guarantees for peak traffic windows — can't have multi-minute tails for triage flows" (CTO, 2026-03-03).

Workshop highlights (dedicated sizing focus):
- Workload mix: chat (40% of requests), embeddings (35%), reranking/batch scoring (25%). Chat avg tokens per response: 180 tokens; embeddings avg tokens: 1024 tokens pre-embedding generation pipeline; reranking typically 3 candidates x 120 tokens each.
- Baseline steady-state: ~18 QPS (requests/sec) across all services during business hours; token profile yields ~3.3k tokens/sec steady-state.
- Peak profile: synchronous peaks 4x steady (scheduled morning surges, marketing-driven campaigns) => peak target ~72 QPS, ~13.2k tokens/sec. Also periodic batch windows overnight for bulk embeddings (18M docs / week).
- Latency SLOs requested: chat p50 < 80ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 350ms for short-turn responses (<=256 tokens); embeddings p95 < 300ms for individual vectorization jobs (note: batching accepted for throughput).
- Desired throughput guarantees: customer wants reserved capacity that supports sustained 5k tokens/sec per reserved GPU cluster slice and ability to burst to 20k tokens/sec across the pool for 5-10 minute windows without degradation.
- GPU sizing asks: initial recommendation from SEs: 4x A100-80GB equiv for baseline steady-state with autoscale policy to add 4 more GPUs for peak (total 8). They prefer a reserved commit for baseline (4 GPUs) + burst pool (shared or guaranteed burst credits). Discussed quantized LLM variants (4-bit/8-bit) to increase tokens/sec while preserving quality.
- Caching/batching opportunities: heavy prefix reuse for triage prompts (~30% reuse) — can reduce effective token compute by ~20% if Redwood prefix caching enabled. Plan: enable KV cache, aggressive prefix reuse for chat to reduce GPU footprint.
- SLA negotiation points: uptime SLA 99.95% for Dedicated control plane; request for explicit p99 latency SLA for chat endpoints during business hours; proposal to include fallback routing to hosted-compatible model variant in SLA for graceful degradation. Also negotiating credit terms for missed SLOs.
- Pricing sensitivity: mid-high; prefer blended reserved + burst pricing. Finance wants 12mo commit but will consider quarterly renewals if SLA + residency clauses satisfied.
- Security/compliance: must support customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS), SSO/SAML with SCIM, audit log retention 1 year, data residency in EU for PHI subset.

POC / Next milestones:
- Deliver sizing workbook (action: Liam) by 2026-03-14 with three reservation tiers (Conservative=4 GPUs, Performance=6 GPUs, High-Availability=8 GPUs) and token/sec modelling per tier.
- Draft Dedicated SLA with latency p99 targets and fallback policy (action: Sofia + Legal) by 2026-03-21.
- Schedule 48h load test in Redwood staging with sample triage workload (action: EmberWave + Redwood SE) target week of 2026-03-28. Need test account, dataset subset, and synthetic traffic script.
- Security review follow-up: provide KMS/HSM architecture diagram and SOC2 evidence (action: Security team) by 2026-03-18.

Blockers and open questions (copied from call notes):
- Q: How does Redwood guarantee p99 latency under noisy neighbors during burst without over-provisioning? Proposed answers to include dedicated reserved slices, strict routing policies, and automatic fallback to cross-region spare pools. Need wording for SLA.
- Q: Can we reserve GPUs in EU region only for PHI workloads? Answer: yes via Private/VPC - need procurement note.
- Finance: need ARR delta between 12mo commit vs 24mo commit (discount bands).
- Ops: clarify maintenance windows and planned upgrade cadence for Dedicated clusters (they want <1% monthly planned downtime).

Audit trail / attachments: see linked_drive_docs for workbook draft + security FAQ. Fireflies call ids above contain action item timestamps.

CRM shorthand lines:
- "CTO cares about p99 — treat as hard req"
- "Prefer reserved baseline, burst credits for events"

- "Agrees to 12mo if SLA includes latency credits & fallback"

Recommended sales play: run a two-week POC (staging load test + one-week pilot in Dedicated reserved baseline) then convert to 12mo committed reserved pool. Emphasize Optimize tooling (batching/caching recs) to show cost delta between reserved levels.
